newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel hails "positive" talks with PLO.
newsitem.headline: Israel hails "positive" talks with PLO.

text.p: Israel and the PLO held talks under U.S. and Egyptian sponsorship on breaking a Middle East peacemaking deadlock which President Bill Clinton said was causing him concern.

"The meeting was effective and it was conducted in a positive and good atmosphere," said a spokesman for Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai, who met Nabil Shaath, Palestinian minister for planning and international cooperation.

The spokesman said "a model for accelerating negotiations" on opening a Palestinian airport in Gaza was agreed at the session at the residence of Egyptian ambassador Mohammad Bassiouny. U.S. ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk also attended.

"Mordechai told Shaath that Israel was prepared for the Palestinian Authority to import electronic equipment for operating the airport but it would not open until security arrangements are set," the spokesman said.
Under interim peace deals with the PLO, Israel has overall control of all border crossings in Gaza and the West Bank.

The spokesman also said Mordechai informed Shaath that Foreign Minister David Levy, Israel's coordinator of peace negotiations would soon approve the start of discussions with the Palestinian Authority on opening a Gaza seaport.
The air and sea ports are issues still outstanding from the interim peace agreements which the PLO has demanded Israel implement.
Formal Israeli-PLO peace talks have been frozen since the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.

"The defence minister stressed that continued progress on matters on the agenda is fully contingent on the Palestinian Authority's determination to fight terrorism and security cooperation with Israel," Mordechai's spokesman said.

There was no immediate PLO comment following the talks which a spokesman for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said had been aimed at finding "a common ground and a way to restore negotiations to their correct path".
At a NATO summit in Madrid, Clinton said he was working on new ideas to get Middle East peacemaking moving again.
"I'm very concerned about what's happening in the peace process. I'm very concerned about the growing tensions between the Palestinians and the Israelis," Clinton told a news conference.
Netanyahu has proposed moving straight into negotiations on a final peace settlement with the Palestinians rather than pursuing crisis-plagued talks on interim issues.

"I believe that contrary to all the detractors and depressing prophecies, our government...can achieve a permanent peace agreement with the Palestinians, on condition they want one," Netanyahu told Israel's Channel One television.

The PLO demands he first halt the settlement-building at Jabal Abu Ghneim, or Har Homa, on Israeli-occupied land in East Jerusalem, before full-fledged talks can resume. Netanyahu has pledged repeatedly to press ahead with the construction.
The PLO has also been cool to Netanyahu's proposal to move into "final-status" talks before implementing the rural redeployment in the West Bank.
Egypt has tried in recent months, with little apparent success, to mediate between the two sides after U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross failed to break the deadlock.

In another sign of Israeli-Palestinian tensions, two Israeli paramilitary border policemen were wounded by a roadside bomb near the self-ruled Arab city of Nablus in the West Bank on Wednesday, the army said.
Shots were fired were fired at a building housing Jewish settlers in the divided West Bank town of Hebron, scene of recent Israeli-Palestinian clashes.
Witnesses and Israeli military sources said no one was hurt but at least one bullet hit an outer wall of the Beit Hadassah settler enclave.
